artifacts.summary: Re-derives every carried cost/count figure (finding several individually stale, dated 2026-10-16/10-19 despite a blanket 2026-11-10 claim), corrects the recursive-meta-suite count from 35 to 14 genuine members after removing comment-only and stub-only false positives, applies the owner's DELETE/KEEP rule to produce a 0-DELETE/14-KEEP verdict table (every genuine recursive meta-suite tests a cross-invocation/crash/concurrency property no single real gate run can self-certify), identifies the actual cost driver for the two most expensive suites as fixed per-invocation verify-deploy.sh overhead rather than gate-8 battery recursion (already stubbed away), confirms no suite-level demotion tier exists (known-failures.txt and --skip-slow/--max-cost are gate-granularity only), and reconfirms the /tmp fixture leak is still live (1,716 entries, 1.4GB) with a recommendation to extend claude-refresh.sh rather than open a separate task.

memory_candidates.content: agent-system/extensions/core run-all.sh/verify-deploy.sh suite-count citations are multi-valued depending on scope: core-only source-store test-*.sh (157 as of 2026-11-17), all-loaded-extensions source-store total (197), the currently-deployed .claude/ tree for a given repo (189 here), and verify-deploy.sh's own live corpus-scan test_suites field (204, a different classification boundary). A bare suite count carried from an earlier measurement is never safe to cite without stating which of these four it means.

verify-deploy.sh's corpus-scan step (scripts=N lines=N test_suites=N md_files=N md_lines=N) runs unconditionally on every invocation regardless of --only-gate scope, costing ~4.6s measured live even for a single-gate selection. A suite that invokes verify-deploy.sh many times via --only-gate (e.g. a cache-equivalence or crash-net regression suite) pays this fixed cost once per invocation; its wall-clock total is often dominated by invocation-count x this fixed overhead rather than by any specific gate's real work. --skip-slow and --max-cost both operate at gate granularity (gate 8 is the only 'slow' gate and is monolithic, all-suites-or-none), so neither can selectively demote one expensive suite inside gate 8's own battery -- a suite-level demotion tier does not exist and would be new machinery.

A lexical grep for 'does this suite mention run-all.sh/verify-deploy.sh' over-counts suites that actually re-invoke those scripts by roughly 2.6x in this corpus: many suites only write an empty stub file with that name for call-counting (test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh) or plant the literal string as synthetic fixture content for a classification lint to detect (test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh), never executing the real script. Before classifying any suite as a 'recursive meta-suite' for a cost or deletion audit, confirm the invocation is real (grep for the variable/literal actually being executed as a command, not just appearing as text) rather than trusting a name-mention grep.
